newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish defence minister on visit to Israel.
newsitem.headline: Turkish defence minister on visit to Israel.

text.p: Turkish Defence Minister Turhan Tayan left on Wednesday for a visit to Israel as part of increasing defence cooperation between the two countries, the state-run Anatolian news agency said.
The trip was a further blow to the prestige of Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan who won elections 16 months ago partly on a promise to cut military ties to the Jewish state.
Tayan, from the secularist wing of Erbakan's coalition government, is to hold talks with his Israeli counterpart and take part in a panel discussion on the Middle East, Anatolian said.
Turkey and Israel have signed defence cooperation agreements which drew an angry response from Iran and many in the Arab world. Israeli planes have flown training flights in Turkey under the accords.
While in Israel, Tayan is to visit Israel Aerospace Industries, which is modernising Turkey's F-4 jet fighters. He is due to return to Turkey on May 2.
Turkey's anti-Islamist army, one of the country's most influential bodies, is pushing Erbakan to curb religious activism.
